   176→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   177→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   178→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   179→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   180→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   181→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   182→//
   183→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   184→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   185→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   186→//   - "merge", "squash", "commit": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated or amend commits)
   187→//
   188→
   189→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   190→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   191→
   192→	// Skip during rebase, cherry-pick, or revert operations
   193→	// These are replaying existing commits and should not be linked to agent sessions
   194→	if isGitSequenceOperation() {
   195→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped during git sequence operation",
   196→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   197→			slog.String("source", source),
   198→		)
   199→		return nil
   200→	}
   201→
   202→	// Skip for merge, squash, and commit (amend) sources
   203→	// These are auto-generated or reusing existing messages - not from Claude sessions
   204→	switch source {
   205→	case "merge", "squash", "commit":
   206→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",
   207→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   208→			slog.String("source", source),
   209→		)
   210→		return nil
   211→	}
   212→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   213→	if err != nil {
   214→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   215→	}
   216→
   217→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   218→	if err != nil {
   219→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   223→	// We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because the user may have made
   224→	// intermediate commits without entering new prompts, causing HEAD to diverge
   225→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   226→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   227→		// No active sessions or error listing - silently skip (hooks must be resilient)
   228→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions",
   229→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   230→			slog.String("source", source),
   231→		)
   232→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   233→	}
   234→
   235→	// Check if any session has new content to condense
   236→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   237→
   238→	// Determine which checkpoint ID to use
   239→	var checkpointID id.CheckpointID
   240→	var hasNewContent bool
   241→	var reusedSession *SessionState
   242→
   243→	if len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   244→		// New content exists - will generate new checkpoint ID below
   245→		hasNewContent = true
   246→	} else {
   247→		// No new content - check if any session has a LastCheckpointID to reuse
   248→		// This handles the case where user splits Claude's work across multiple commits
   249→		// Reuse if: LastCheckpointID exists AND (FilesTouched is empty OR files overlap)
   250→		// - FilesTouched empty: commits made before session stop, reuse checkpoint
   251→		// - FilesTouched populated: only reuse if files overlap (prevents unrelated commits from reusing)
   252→
   253→		// Get current HEAD to filter sessions
   254→		head, err := repo.Head()
   255→		if err != nil {
   256→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   257→		}
   258→		currentHeadHash := head.Hash().String()
   259→
   260→		// Filter to sessions where BaseCommit matches current HEAD
   261→		// This prevents reusing checkpoint IDs from old sessions
   262→		// Note: BaseCommit is kept current both when new content is condensed (in the
   263→		// condensation process) and when no new content is found (via PostCommit when
   264→		// reusing checkpoint IDs). If none match, we don't add a trailer rather than
   265→		// falling back to old sessions which could have stale checkpoint IDs.
   266→		var currentSessions []*SessionState
   267→		for _, session := range sessions {
   268→			if session.BaseCommit == currentHeadHash {
   269→				currentSessions = append(currentSessions, session)
   270→			}
   271→		}
   272→
   273→		if len(currentSessions) == 0 {
   274→			// No sessions match current HEAD - don't try to reuse checkpoint IDs
   275→			// from old sessions as they may be stale
   276→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no sessions match current HEAD",
   277→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   278→				slog.String("source", source),
   279→				slog.String("current_head", currentHeadHash[:7]),
   280→				slog.Int("total_sessions", len(sessions)),
   281→			)
   282→			return nil
   283→		}
   284→
   285→		stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
   286→		for _, session := range currentSessions {
   287→			if !session.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() &&
   288→				(len(session.FilesTouched) == 0 || hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, session.FilesTouched)) {
   289→				checkpointID = session.LastCheckpointID
   290→				reusedSession = session
   291→				break
   292→			}
   293→		}
   294→		if checkpointID.IsEmpty() {
   295→			// No new content and no previous checkpoint to reference (or staged files are unrelated)
   296→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no content to link",
   297→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   298→				slog.String("source", source),
   299→				slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   300→				slog.Int("sessions_with_content", len(sessionsWithContent)),
   301→			)
   302→			return nil
   303→		}
   304→	}
   305→
   306→	// Read current commit message
   307→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   308→	if err != nil {
   309→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   310→	}
   311→
   312→	message := string(content)
   313→
   314→	// Get or generate checkpoint ID (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   315→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   316→		// Trailer already exists (e.g., amend) - keep it
   317→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer already exists",
   318→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   319→			slog.String("source", source),
   320→			slog.String("existing_checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   321→		)
   322→		return nil
   323→	}
   324→
   325→	if hasNewContent {
   326→		// New content: generate new checkpoint ID
   327→		cpID, err := id.Generate()
   328→		if err != nil {
   329→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   330→		}
   331→		checkpointID = cpID
   332→	}
   333→	// Otherwise checkpointID is already set to LastCheckpointID from above
   334→
   335→	// Determine agent type and last prompt from session
   336→	agentType := DefaultAgentType // default for backward compatibility
   337→	var lastPrompt string
   338→	if hasNewContent && len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   339→		session := sessionsWithContent[0]
   340→		if session.AgentType != "" {
   341→			agentType = session.AgentType
   342→		}
   343→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, session)
   344→	} else if reusedSession != nil {
   345→		// Reusing checkpoint from existing session - get agent type and prompt from that session
   346→		if reusedSession.AgentType != "" {
   347→			agentType = reusedSession.AgentType
   348→		}
   349→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, reusedSession)
   350→	}
   351→
   352→	// Prepare prompt for display: collapse newlines/whitespace, then truncate (rune-safe)
   353→	displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(lastPrompt), 80, "...")
   354→
   355→	// Add trailer differently based on commit source
   356→	if source == "message" {
   357→		// Using -m or -F: ask user interactively whether to add trailer
   358→		// (comments won't be stripped by git in this mode)
   359→
   360→		// Build context string for interactive prompt
   361→		var promptContext string
   362→		if displayPrompt != "" {
   363→			promptContext = "You have an active " + string(agentType) + " session.\nLast Prompt: " + displayPrompt
   364→		}
   365→
   366→		if !askConfirmTTY("Link this commit to "+string(agentType)+" session context?", promptContext, true) {
   367→			// User declined - don't add trailer
   368→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   369→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   370→				slog.String("source", source),
   371→			)
   372→			return nil
   373→		}
   374→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   375→	} else {
   376→		// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   377→		message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   378→	}
   379→
   380→	logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   381→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   382→		slog.String("source", source),
   383→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   384→		slog.Bool("has_new_content", hasNewContent),
   385→	)
   386→
   387→	// Write updated message back
   388→	if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   389→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   390→	}
   391→
   392→	return nil
   393→}
   394→
   395→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   396→// Checks if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer and if so, condenses
   397→// session data from shadow branches to entire/sessions.
   398→// If the user removed the trailer during commit message editing, this is treated
   399→// as a "manual" commit and no condensation happens.
   400→//
   401→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   402→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostCommit() error {
   403→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   404→
   405→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   406→	if err != nil {
   407→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   408→	}
   409→
   410→	// Get HEAD commit to check for trailer
   411→	head, err := repo.Head()
   412→	if err != nil {
   413→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   414→	}
   415→
   416→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   417→	if err != nil {
   418→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   419→	}
   420→
   421→	// Check if commit has checkpoint trailer (ParseCheckpoint validates format)
   422→	checkpointID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(commit.Message)
   423→	if !found {
   424→		// No trailer - user removed it, treat as manual commit
   425→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no checkpoint trailer",
   426→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   427→		)
   428→		return nil
   429→	}
   430→
   431→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   432→	if err != nil {
   433→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   434→	}
   435→
   436→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   437→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   438→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   439→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: no active sessions despite trailer",
   440→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   441→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   442→		)
   443→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   444→	}
   445→
   446→	// Filter to sessions with new content
   447→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   448→	if len(sessionsWithContent) == 0 {
   449→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no new content to condense",
   450→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   451→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   452→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   453→		)
   454→		// Still update BaseCommit for all sessions in this worktree
   455→		// This prevents stale BaseCommit when commits happen without condensation
   456→		// (e.g., when reusing a previous checkpoint ID for split commits)
   457→		newHead := head.Hash().String()
   458→		for _, state := range sessions {
   459→			if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   460→				state.BaseCommit = newHead
   461→				if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   462→					logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: failed to update session BaseCommit",
   463→						slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   464→						slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   465→					)
   466→				}
   467→			}
   468→		}
   469→		return nil
   470→	}
   471→
   472→	// Track shadow branch names to clean up after successful condensation
   473→	shadowBranchesToDelete := make(map[string]struct{})
   474→
   475→	// Condense sessions that have new content
   476→	for _, state := range sessionsWithContent {
   477→		// Compute shadow branch name BEFORE condensation modifies state.BaseCommit
   478→		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   479→
   480→		result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
   481→		if err != nil {
   482→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: condensation failed for session %s: %v\n",
   483→				state.SessionID, err)
   484→			continue
   485→		}
   486→
   487→		// Track this shadow branch for cleanup
   488→		shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName] = struct{}{}
   489→
   490→		// Update session state for the new base commit
   491→		// After condensation, the session continues from the NEW commit (HEAD), so we:
   492→		// 1. Update BaseCommit to new HEAD - session now tracks from new commit
   493→		// 2. Reset StepCount to 0 - no checkpoints exist on new shadow branch yet
   494→		// 3. Update CheckpointTranscriptStart - track transcript position for detecting new content
   495→		// 4. Clear PromptAttributions - they were already used in condensation, reset for next cycle
   496→		//
   497→		// This is critical: if we don't update BaseCommit, listAllSessionStates will try
   498→		// to find shadow branch for old commit (which gets deleted), and since StepCount > 0,
   499→		// it will clean up (delete) the session state file. By updating to new HEAD with
   500→		// StepCount = 0, the session is preserved even without a shadow branch.
   501→		state.BaseCommit = head.Hash().String()
   502→		state.StepCount = 0
   503→		state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   504→
   505→		// Clear attribution tracking - condensation already used these values
   506→		// If we don't clear them, they'll be double-counted in the next condensation
   507→		state.PromptAttributions = nil
   508→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   509→
   510→		// Save checkpoint ID so subsequent commits without new content can reuse it
   511→		state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   512→
   513→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   514→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", err)
   515→		}
   516→
   517→		shortID := state.SessionID
   518→		if len(shortID) > 8 {
   519→			shortID = shortID[:8]
   520→		}
   521→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Condensed session %s: %s (%d checkpoints)\n",
   522→			shortID, result.CheckpointID, result.CheckpointsCount)
   523→
   524→		// Log condensation
   525→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   526→		logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed",
   527→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   528→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   529→			slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   530→			slog.Int("transcript_lines", result.TotalTranscriptLines),
   531→		)
   532→	}
   533→
   534→	// Clean up shadow branches after successful condensation
   535→	// Data is now preserved on entire/sessions, so shadow branches are no longer needed
   536→	for shadowBranchName := range shadowBranchesToDelete {
   537→		if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
   538→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to clean up %s: %v\n", shadowBranchName, err)
   539→		} else {
   540→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Cleaned up shadow branch: %s\n", shadowBranchName)
   541→
   542→			// Log branch cleanup
   543→			logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   544→			logging.Info(logCtx, "shadow branch deleted",
   545→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   546→				slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   547→			)
   548→		}
   549→	}
   550→
   551→	return nil
   552→}
   553→
   554→// filterSessionsWithNewContent returns sessions that have new transcript content
   555→// beyond what was already condensed.
   556→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo *git.Repository, sessions []*SessionState) []*SessionState {
   557→	var result []*SessionState
   558→
   559→	for _, state := range sessions {
   560→		hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
   561→		if err != nil {
   562→			// On error, include the session (fail open for hooks)
   563→			result = append(result, state)
   564→			continue
   565→		}
   566→		if hasNew {
   567→			result = append(result, state)
   568→		}
   569→	}
   570→
   571→	return result
   572→}
   573→
   574→// sessionHasNewContent checks if a session has new transcript content
   575→// beyond what was already condensed.
   576→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   577→	// Get shadow branch
   578→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   579→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   580→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   581→	if err != nil {
   582→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   583→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   584→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.
   585→		return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   589→	if err != nil {
   590→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   591→	}
   592→
   593→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   594→	if err != nil {
   595→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   596→	}
   597→
   598→	// Look for transcript file
   599→	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
   600→	var transcriptLines int
   601→
   602→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   603→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   604→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   605→		}
   606→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   607→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   608→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   609→		}
   610→	}
   611→
   612→	// Has new content if there are more lines than already condensed
   613→	return transcriptLines > state.CheckpointTranscriptStart, nil
   614→}
   615→
   616→// countTranscriptLines counts lines in a transcript, matching the counting method used
   617→// in extractSessionData for consistency. This trims trailing empty lines (from final \n
   618→// in JSONL) but includes empty lines in the middle of the file.
   619→func countTranscriptLines(content string) int {
   620→	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   621→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   622→	for len(lines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[len(lines)-1]) == "" {
   623→		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1]
   624→	}
   625→	return len(lines)
   626→}
   627→
   628→// sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript checks if a session has new content
   629→// by examining the live transcript file. This is used when no shadow branch exists
   630→// (i.e., no Stop has happened yet) but the agent may have done work.
   631→//
   632→// Returns true if:
   633→//  1. The transcript has grown since the last condensation, AND
   634→//  2. The new transcript portion contains file modifications, AND
   635→//  3. At least one modified file overlaps with the currently staged files
   636→//
   637→// The overlap check ensures we don't add checkpoint trailers to commits that are
   638→// unrelated to the agent's recent changes.
   639→//
   640→// This handles the scenario where the agent commits mid-session before Stop.
   641→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   642→	// Need both transcript path and agent type to analyze
   643→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" || state.AgentType == "" {
   644→		return false, nil
   645→	}
   646→
   647→	// Get the agent for transcript analysis
   648→	ag, err := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType)
   649→	if err != nil {
   650→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Unknown agent type, fail gracefully
   651→	}
   652→
   653→	// Cast to TranscriptAnalyzer
   654→	analyzer, ok := ag.(agent.TranscriptAnalyzer)
   655→	if !ok {
   656→		return false, nil // Agent doesn't support transcript analysis
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	// Get current transcript position
   660→	currentPos, err := analyzer.GetTranscriptPosition(state.TranscriptPath)
   661→	if err != nil {
   662→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error reading transcript, fail gracefully
   663→	}
   664→
   665→	// Check if transcript has grown since last condensation
   666→	if currentPos <= state.CheckpointTranscriptStart {
   667→		return false, nil // No new content
   668→	}
   669→
   670→	// Transcript has grown - check if there are file modifications in the new portion
   671→	modifiedFiles, _, err := analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   672→	if err != nil {
   673→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error parsing transcript, fail gracefully
   674→	}
   675→
   676→	// No file modifications means no new content to checkpoint
   677→	if len(modifiedFiles) == 0 {
   678→		return false, nil
   679→	}
   680→
   681→	// Check if any modified files overlap with currently staged files
   682→	// This ensures we only add checkpoint trailers to commits that include
   683→	// files the agent actually modified
   684→	stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo) // TODO: does it work? Do we have staged files if this is called at post-commit hook ?
   685→	if !hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, modifiedFiles) {
   686→		return false, nil // No overlap - staged files are unrelated to agent's work
   687→	}
   688→
   689→	return true, nil
   690→}

   692→// addCheckpointTrailer adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer to a commit message.
   693→// Handles proper trailer formatting (blank line before trailers if needed).
   694→func addCheckpointTrailer(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) string {
   695→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   696→
   697→	// If message already ends with trailers (lines starting with key:), just append
   698→	// Otherwise, add a blank line first
   699→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), "\n")
   700→
   701→	// Check if last non-empty, non-comment line looks like a trailer
   702→	// Git comment lines start with # and may contain ": " (e.g., "# Changes to be committed:")
   703→	hasTrailers := false
   704→	for i := len(lines) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   705→		line := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   706→		if line == "" {
   707→			break
   708→		}
   709→		// Skip git comment lines
   710→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   711→			continue
   712→		}
   713→		if strings.Contains(line, ": ") {
   714→			hasTrailers = true
   715→			break
   716→		}
   717→		// Non-comment, non-trailer line found - no existing trailers
   718→		break
   719→	}
   720→
   721→	if hasTrailers {
   722→		// Append trailer directly
   723→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n" + trailer + "\n"
   724→	}
   725→
   726→	// Add blank line before trailer
   727→	return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n"
   728→}

   730→// addCheckpointTrailerWithComment adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer with an explanatory comment.
   731→// The trailer is placed above the git comment block but below the user's message area,
   732→// with a comment explaining that the user can remove it if they don't want to link the commit
   733→// to the agent session. If prompt is non-empty, it's shown as context.
   734→func addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, agentName, prompt string) string {
   735→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   736→	commentLines := []string{
   737→		"# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link this commit to " + agentName + " session context.",
   738→	}
   739→	if prompt != "" {
   740→		commentLines = append(commentLines, "# Last Prompt: "+prompt)
   741→	}
   742→	commentLines = append(commentLines, "# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.")
   743→	comment := strings.Join(commentLines, "\n")
   744→
   745→	lines := strings.Split(message, "\n")
   746→
   747→	// Find where the git comment block starts (first # line)
   748→	commentStart := -1
   749→	for i, line := range lines {
   750→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   751→			commentStart = i
   752→			break
   753→		}
   754→	}
   755→
   756→	if commentStart == -1 {
   757→		// No git comments, append trailer at the end
   758→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n"
   759→	}
   760→
   761→	// Split into user content and git comments
   762→	userContent := strings.Join(lines[:commentStart], "\n")
   763→	gitComments := strings.Join(lines[commentStart:], "\n")
   764→
   765→	// Build result: user content, blank line, trailer, comment, blank line, git comments
   766→	userContent = strings.TrimRight(userContent, "\n")
   767→	if userContent == "" {
   768→		// No user content yet - leave space for them to type, then trailer
   769→		// Two newlines: first for user's message line, second for blank separator
   770→		return "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   771→	}
   772→	return userContent + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   773→}

   775→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
   776→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.

   805→		if state.AgentType == "" && agentType != "" {
   806→			state.AgentType = agentType

   811→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
   812→		}

   814→		// Clear LastCheckpointID on every new prompt
   815→		// This is set during PostCommit when a checkpoint is created, and should be
   816→		// cleared when the user enters a new prompt (starting fresh work)
   817→		if state.LastCheckpointID != "" {
   818→			state.LastCheckpointID = ""
   819→		}
   820→
   821→		// Calculate attribution at prompt start (BEFORE agent makes any changes)
   822→		// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint (or base commit for first prompt).
   823→		// IMPORTANT: Always calculate attribution, even for the first checkpoint, to capture
   824→		// user edits made before the first prompt. The inner CalculatePromptAttribution handles
   825→		// nil lastCheckpointTree by falling back to baseTree.
   826→		promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   827→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr

   830→		// migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded handles renaming the shadow branch and updating state.BaseCommit
   831→		if _, err := s.migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded(repo, state); err != nil {
   832→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check/migrate shadow branch: %w", err)
   833→		}

   836→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
   837→		}
   838→		return nil
   839→	}

   841→	// Continue below to properly initialize it
   842→

   844→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath)
   845→	if err != nil {
   846→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
   847→	}
   848→

   850→	result := session.Transition(state.Phase, session.EventTurnStart, session.TransitionContext{})
   851→	session.ApplyCommonActions(state, result)

   854→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
   855→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   856→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr

   858→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
   859→	}

   862→	return nil
   863→}

   865→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
   866→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
   867→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
   868→//
   869→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   870→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
   871→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
   872→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
   873→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
   874→	repo *git.Repository,
   875→	state *SessionState,
   876→) PromptAttribution {
   877→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   878→	nextCheckpointNum := state.StepCount + 1
   879→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
   880→
   881→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
   882→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
   883→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
   884→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
   885→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   886→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   887→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   888→	if err != nil {
   889→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
   890→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
   891→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   892→	} else {
   893→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   894→		if err != nil {
   895→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
   896→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
   897→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   898→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   899→		} else {
   900→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
   901→			if err != nil {
   902→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
   903→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   904→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   905→			}
   906→		}
   907→	}
   908→
   909→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
   910→	var baseTree *object.Tree
   911→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
   912→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
   913→			baseTree = tree
   914→		} else {
   915→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base tree unavailable",
   916→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   917→		}
   918→	} else {
   919→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base commit unavailable",
   920→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
   921→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   922→	}
   923→
   924→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   925→	if err != nil {
   926→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree",
   927→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   928→		return result
   929→	}
   930→
   931→	// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files
   932→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   933→	if err != nil {
   934→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree status",
   935→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   936→		return result
   937→	}
   938→
   939→	worktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()
   940→
   941→	// Build map of changed files with their worktree content
   942→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   943→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
   944→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
   945→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {
   946→		// Skip unmodified files
   947→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {
   948→			continue
   949→		}
   950→		// Skip .entire metadata directory (session data, not user code)
   951→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {
   952→			continue
   953→		}
   954→
   955→		// Always read from worktree to match checkpoint behavior
   956→		fullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)
   957→		var content string
   958→		if data, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // filePath is from git worktree status
   959→			// Use git's binary detection algorithm (matches getFileContent behavior).
   960→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.
   961→			isBinary, binErr := binary.IsBinary(bytes.NewReader(data))
   962→			if binErr == nil && !isBinary {
   963→				content = string(data)
   964→			}
   965→		}
   966→		// else: file deleted, unreadable, or binary - content remains empty string
   967→
   968→		changedFiles[filePath] = content
   969→	}
   970→
   971→	// Use CalculatePromptAttribution from manual_commit_attribution.go
   972→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)
   973→
   974→	return result
   975→}

   977→// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit.
   978→func getStagedFiles(repo *git.Repository) []string {
   979→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   980→	if err != nil {
   981→		return nil
   982→	}
   983→
   984→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   985→	if err != nil {
   986→		return nil
   987→	}
   988→
   989→	var staged []string
   990→	for path, fileStatus := range status {
   991→		// Check if file is staged (in index)
   992→		if fileStatus.Staging != git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging != git.Untracked {
   993→			staged = append(staged, path)
   994→		}
   995→	}
   996→	return staged
   997→}

  1020→// hasOverlappingFiles checks if any file in stagedFiles appears in filesTouched.
  1021→func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
  1022→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1023→	for _, f := range filesTouched {

  1025→	}
  1026→
  1027→	for _, staged := range stagedFiles {
  1028→		if touchedSet[staged] {
  1029→			return true
  1030→		}
  1031→	}
  1032→	return false

   157→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.

   159→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
   160→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.

   184→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   185→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   186→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   187→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   188→
   189→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   190→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   191→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   192→	}
   193→
   194→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   195→
   196→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   197→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   198→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   199→	}
   200→	if err != nil {
   201→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   202→	}
   203→
   204→	var state State
   205→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   206→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   207→	}
   208→	state.NormalizeAfterLoad()
   209→	return &state, nil
   210→}

   212→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   213→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   214→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   215→
   216→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   217→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   218→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   222→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   226→	if err != nil {
   227→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   231→
   232→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   233→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   234→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   235→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   236→	}
   237→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   238→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→	return nil
   241→}

   243→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   244→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   245→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   246→
   247→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   248→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   249→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   250→	}
   251→
   252→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   253→
   254→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   255→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   256→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   257→		}

   272→// List returns all session states.
   273→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   274→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   275→
   276→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   277→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   278→		return nil, nil
   279→	}
   280→	if err != nil {
   281→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	var states []*State
   285→	for _, entry := range entries {
   286→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   287→			continue
   288→		}
   289→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   290→			continue // Skip temp files
   291→		}
   292→
   293→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   294→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   295→		if err != nil {
   296→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   297→		}
   298→		if state == nil {
   299→			continue
   300→		}
   301→
   302→		states = append(states, state)
   303→	}
   304→	return states, nil
   305→}

   307→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   308→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   309→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   310→}

   312→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   313→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   314→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   315→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   316→	ctx := context.Background()
   317→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   318→	cmd.Dir = "."
   319→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   320→	if err != nil {
   321→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   322→	}
   323→
   324→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   325→
   326→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   327→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   328→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   329→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   330→	}
   331→
   332→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   333→}

    58→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) listAllSessionStates() ([]*SessionState, error) {

    65→	if err != nil {

    81→

    83→		// Only cleanup if the session has created checkpoints (StepCount > 0)
    84→		// AND has no LastCheckpointID (not recently condensed)

    16→	// MetadataTrailerKey points to the metadata directory within a commit tree.

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromPendingCheckpointID verifies the main
// bug fix: when a user does `git commit --amend -m "new message"`, the Entire-Checkpoint
// trailer is lost because the new message has no trailer. PrepareCommitMsg should restore
// the trailer from PendingCheckpointID in session state.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromPendingCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-restore"
	err := s.InitializeSession(sessionID, "Claude Code", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Simulate the state after a condensation: PendingCheckpointID is set
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	state.PendingCheckpointID = "abc123def456"
	err = s.saveSessionState(state)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer (user did --amend -m "new message")
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "New amended message\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - trailer should be restored from PendingCheckpointID
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found,
		"trailer should be restored from PendingCheckpointID on amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"restored trailer should use PendingCheckpointID value")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoPendingID verifies that when amending with
// no existing trailer and no PendingCheckpointID in session state, no trailer is added.
// This is the case where the session has never been condensed.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoPendingID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-no-id"
	err := s.InitializeSession(sessionID, "Claude Code", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify PendingCheckpointID is empty (default)
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	assert.Empty(t, state.PendingCheckpointID, "PendingCheckpointID should be empty by default")

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "Amended without any session context\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - no trailer should be added
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"no trailer should be added when PendingCheckpointID is empty")

	// Message should be unchanged
	assert.Equal(t, newMsg, string(content),
		"commit message should be unchanged when no trailer to restore")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_NormalCommitUsesPendingCheckpointID verifies that during
// a normal commit (source=""), if the session has a PendingCheckpointID set,
// it is used instead of generating a new random checkpoint ID.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_NormalCommitUsesPendingCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-normal-pending"
	err := s.InitializeSession(sessionID, "Claude Code", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Create a checkpoint so the session has content on the shadow branch
	err = createTestCheckpoint(t, dir, s, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Set the session to ACTIVE_COMMITTED with a PendingCheckpointID
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	state.Phase = session.PhaseActiveCommitted
	state.PendingCheckpointID = "fedcba987654"
	err = s.saveSessionState(state)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file with no trailer (normal editor flow)
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	normalMsg := "Feature: add new functionality\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(normalMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="" (normal commit, editor flow)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - trailer should use PendingCheckpointID
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found,
		"trailer should be present for normal commit with active session content")
	assert.Equal(t, "fedcba987654", cpID.String(),
		"normal commit should reuse PendingCheckpointID instead of generating a new one")
}

// createTestCheckpoint creates a minimal checkpoint on the shadow branch so that
// the session appears to have content. This writes a test file change and saves
// a checkpoint via the strategy.
func createTestCheckpoint(t *testing.T, repoDir string, s *ManualCommitStrategy, sessionID string) error {
	t.Helper()

	// Modify a file in the working tree to create "dirty" state
	testFile := filepath.Join(repoDir, "test.txt")
	if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte("modified content"), 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Stage the change so it appears in git status
	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(repoDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := wt.Add("test.txt"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Use SaveChanges to create a real checkpoint on the shadow branch
	ctx := SaveContext{
		SessionID:      sessionID,
		AgentType:      "Claude Code",
		Transcript:     []byte(`{"type":"message","role":"assistant"}`),
		TranscriptPath: "",
	}
	return s.SaveChanges(ctx)
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer verifies that when amending
// a commit that already has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, the trailer is preserved
// unchanged. source="commit" indicates an amend operation.
//
// This currently FAILS because PrepareCommitMsg returns early for source="commit"
// before checking the existing message. In this case the file is unchanged, so the
// trailer IS preserved -- but only by accident (the early return does not modify the
// file). The fix should explicitly handle this case.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-preserve"
	err := s.InitializeSession(sessionID, "Claude Code", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file that already has the trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	existingMsg := "Original commit message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: abc123def456\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(existingMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back and verify the trailer is still present
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found, "trailer should still be present after amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"trailer should preserve the original checkpoint ID")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromPendingCheckpointID verifies the main

//
// This FAILS because PrepareCommitMsg currently returns early for source="commit",

func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromPendingCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-restore"
	err := s.InitializeSession(sessionID, "Claude Code", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Simulate state after condensation: PendingCheckpointID is set
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	state.PendingCheckpointID = "abc123def456"
	err = s.saveSessionState(state)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer (user did --amend -m "new message")
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "New amended message\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - trailer should be restored from PendingCheckpointID
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found,
		"trailer should be restored from PendingCheckpointID on amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"restored trailer should use PendingCheckpointID value")

// createShadowBranchWithTranscript creates a shadow branch commit with a minimal
// transcript file so that filterSessionsWithNewContent detects new content.
// This uses low-level go-git plumbing to create the branch directly.
func createShadowBranchWithTranscript(t *testing.T, repoDir string, sessionID string) {
	t.Helper()

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(repoDir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	head, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	baseCommit := head.Hash().String()

	// Build the tree with a transcript file at the expected path
	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + sessionID
	transcriptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
	transcriptContent := `{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":"hello"}` + "\n"

	// Create blob for transcript
	blobObj := &plumbing.MemoryObject{}
	blobObj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
	blobObj.SetSize(int64(len(transcriptContent)))
	writer, err := blobObj.Writer()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = writer.Write([]byte(transcriptContent))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, writer.Close())

	blobHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(blobObj)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Build nested tree structure: .entire/metadata/<sessionID>/full.jsonl
	// We need to build trees bottom-up
	innerTree := object.Tree{
		Entries: []object.TreeEntry{
			{Name: paths.TranscriptFileName, Mode: 0o100644, Hash: blobHash},
		},
	}
	innerTreeObj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
	innerTreeObj.SetType(plumbing.TreeObject)
	require.NoError(t, innerTree.Encode(innerTreeObj))
	innerTreeHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(innerTreeObj)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Build .entire/metadata/<sessionID> level
	sessionTree := object.Tree{
		Entries: []object.TreeEntry{
			{Name: sessionID, Mode: 0o040000, Hash: innerTreeHash},
		},
	}
	sessionTreeObj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
	sessionTreeObj.SetType(plumbing.TreeObject)
	require.NoError(t, sessionTree.Encode(sessionTreeObj))
	sessionTreeHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(sessionTreeObj)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Build .entire/metadata level
	metadataTree := object.Tree{
		Entries: []object.TreeEntry{
			{Name: "metadata", Mode: 0o040000, Hash: sessionTreeHash},
		},
	}
	metadataTreeObj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
	metadataTreeObj.SetType(plumbing.TreeObject)
	require.NoError(t, metadataTree.Encode(metadataTreeObj))
	metadataTreeHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(metadataTreeObj)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Build .entire level
	entireTree := object.Tree{
		Entries: []object.TreeEntry{
			{Name: ".entire", Mode: 0o040000, Hash: metadataTreeHash},
		},
	}
	entireTreeObj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
	entireTreeObj.SetType(plumbing.TreeObject)
	require.NoError(t, entireTree.Encode(entireTreeObj))
	entireTreeHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(entireTreeObj)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Create commit on shadow branch
	now := time.Now()
	commitObj := &object.Commit{
		Author: object.Signature{
			Name:  "Test",
			Email: "test@test.com",
			When:  now,
		},
		Committer: object.Signature{
			Name:  "Test",
			Email: "test@test.com",
			When:  now,
		},
		Message:  "checkpoint\n\nEntire-Metadata: " + metadataDir + "\nEntire-Session: " + sessionID + "\nEntire-Strategy: manual-commit\n",
		TreeHash: entireTreeHash,
	}
	commitEnc := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
	require.NoError(t, commitObj.Encode(commitEnc))
	commitHash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(commitEnc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Create the shadow branch reference
	// WorktreeID is empty for main worktree, which matches what setupGitRepo creates
	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, "")
	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
	ref := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(ref))

	// Verify the transcript is readable
	verifyCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(commitHash)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	verifyTree, err := verifyCommit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	file, err := verifyTree.File(transcriptPath)
	require.NoError(t, err, "transcript file should exist at %s", transcriptPath)
	content, err := file.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotEmpty(t, content, "transcript should have content")
}

## Task 6: Phase-Aware PrepareCommitMsg + Amend Fix (PR 3)

Update `PrepareCommitMsg()` to use `PendingCheckpointID` from session state and fix the
`git commit --amend` trailer loss bug.

**Files:**
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` — `PrepareCommitMsg()`: use PendingCheckpointID, fix amend handling

**Logic:**
```
# Rebase/merge: skip entirely (existing behavior)
if source == "merge" or "squash":
    return

# Amend: preserve or restore trailer
if source == "commit":
    if message already has Entire-Checkpoint trailer:
        return (keep it)
    if any session has PendingCheckpointID:
        add trailer with PendingCheckpointID
        return
    return (no checkpoint to link)

# Normal commit (existing behavior + PendingCheckpointID)
if any session is ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED with PendingCheckpointID:
    use it
else if sessions have new content:
    generate new PendingCheckpointID, store in state
    use it
else if sessions have LastCheckpointID:
    reuse it
```

**Current bug fixed:** PrepareCommitMsg previously returned early for `source="commit"`
(amend), skipping entirely. Code to preserve existing trailers was unreachable. When users
amended with `-m`, the trailer was lost. Now PendingCheckpointID in session state is the
source of truth, and the trailer is restored even if `-m` strips it.

**Verification:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test`

Remove legacy single-session tracking.

- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_geminicli_handlers.go` — Remove `paths.ReadCurrentSession()` usage
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_git_cmd.go` — `initHookLogging()`: get session ID from session state files instead
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/debug.go` — `debugShowCommand`: list active sessions from StateStore instead
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go` — Remove `ReadCurrentSession()`, `WriteCurrentSession()`, `CurrentSessionFile`
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths_test.go` — Remove related tests
- Update any other tests referencing current_session

**Verification:** `mise run test:ci`

`ApplyCommonActions` doesn't clear `PendingCheckpointID`. The `InitializeSession` flow calls `session.Transition(state.Phase, session.EventTurnStart, ...)` and `session.ApplyCommonActions()`. But neither clears `PendingCheckpointID`.

Looking at the test flow:
1. First commit → PostCommit sets `PendingCheckpointID` during condensation
2. `SimulateUserPromptSubmit` → calls `InitializeSession` → transitions phase but doesn't clear `PendingCheckpointID`
3. Second commit → PrepareCommitMsg finds `PendingCheckpointID` and reuses it (BUG)

The fix should be to clear `PendingCheckpointID` when a new turn starts (EventTurnStart). This is conceptually correct: when a new prompt arrives, any pending checkpoint from a previous commit cycle should be cleared because the new work should get a fresh checkpoint ID.

The cleanest place to clear it is in `ApplyCommonActions` when `ActionUpdateLastInteraction` fires (which happens on every turn start). But that would couple the session package to the `PendingCheckpointID` concept, which is strategy-specific.

Actually, looking more carefully at where `PendingCheckpointID` is defined — it's on `session.State` itself (line 51-53 in `session/state.go`), so it's already part of the session package. The most natural fix is to clear it in `InitializeSession` when a new turn starts.

I understand the issue now. The test flow:

1. Session starts, two prompts, Stop → checkpoint on shadow branch
2. First commit → PostCommit condensation → sets `PendingCheckpointID` (my change)  
3. Continue session (no `SimulateUserPromptSubmit`) → third prompt → Stop → new checkpoint
4. Second commit → PrepareCommitMsg finds `PendingCheckpointID` → **reuses it** (WRONG — should generate new ID because there's NEW content to condense)

The problem is that `PendingCheckpointID` should be reused for the **same content** (e.g., amend), but when there's NEW content since the last condensation, a new ID should be generated.

Looking at the logic more carefully: `PendingCheckpointID` is meant for the amend case (restoring a trailer that was lost). For normal commits with new content, it should only be reused if there's NO new content beyond what was already condensed. But in this case, there IS new content (the third prompt created a new checkpoint on the shadow branch).

The fix: I need to reconsider when to reuse `PendingCheckpointID`. It should be used:
- **For amend** (`source="commit"`): always (this is the main use case)
- **For normal commits** with new content: only if it's the same content (i.e., the `PendingCheckpointID` was set and no new checkpoints were added after it)

Actually, thinking about it more carefully, the simplest correct approach is:
- `PendingCheckpointID` should be cleared when new content is saved (i.e., when `SaveChanges`/`SaveTaskCheckpoint` creates a new checkpoint on the shadow branch), because new content means a new checkpoint cycle.
- It should also be cleared on `InitializeSession` (new prompt).

But `PendingCheckpointID` is set by PostCommit (during condensation), and new content arrives via `SimulateStop` → `SaveChanges`. The flow in the failing test:

1. SaveChanges (checkpoint 1) → PendingCheckpointID empty
2. Commit → PostCommit sets PendingCheckpointID  
3. SaveChanges (checkpoint 2 — new content!) → PendingCheckpointID should be cleared here
4. Commit → PrepareCommitMsg should generate new ID

So the fix is to clear `PendingCheckpointID` in `SaveChanges` when a new checkpoint is created. Let me find where `SaveChanges` updates state.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/alex/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/4.2.0/skills/requesting-code-review

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or origin/main
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code-reviewer subagent:**

Use Task tool with superpowers:code-reviewer type, fill template at `code-reviewer.md`

**Placeholders:**
- `{WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED}` - What you just built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | awk '{print }')
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent]
  WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED: Verification and repair functions for conversation index
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Integration with Workflows

**Subagent-Driven Development:**
- Review after EACH task
- Catch issues before they compound
- Fix before moving to next task

**Executing Plans:**
- Review after each batch (3 tasks)
- Get feedback, apply, continue

**Ad-Hoc Development:**
- Review before merge
- Review when stuck

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md
Let me gather the git SHAs and dispatch the code reviewer.

1→# Session Phase State Machine — Review Notes
     2→
     3→Review of `docs/plans/2026-02-06-session-phase-state-machine.md`.
     4→
     5→## Decisions
     6→
     7→### TTL Removal
     8→
     9→**Decision: Remove TTL entirely from the design.**
    10→
    11→- No TTL in PostCommit. ACTIVE → ACTIVE_COMMITTED always defers, no time-based heuristic.
    12→- No TTL in SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit. No auto-condensation of stale sessions from other sessions.
    13→- No TIMED_OUT virtual state. Remove tiered TTL section from plan.
    14→- No PID tracking. User is the oracle for session liveness.
    15→
    16→**Rationale:**
    17→- TTL in PostCommit causes false positives (long builds, permission prompts, complex reasoning).
    18→- Auto-condensing stale sessions during unrelated sessions breaks temporal locality and confuses users.
    19→- The only scenario requiring active detection (ACTIVE_COMMITTED + dead agent) is rare enough to handle manually.
    20→
    21→### `LastInteractionTime` Updates
    22→
    23→**Decision: Update `LastInteractionTime` on every hook invocation.**
    24→
    25→- UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse — all of them.
    26→- Provides accurate "last seen" signal for staleness detection.
    27→- Helps identify forgotten terminals (e.g., agent waiting on permission prompt).
    28→
    29→### Session Health / Doctor Command
    30→
    31→**Decision: Add `entire sessions fix` command + SessionStart warning.**
    32→
    33→- SessionStart: warn if sessions exist with no interaction in ~hours.
    34→  - Covers both stuck ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions AND forgotten terminals.
    35→  - No auto-healing, just a notice with actionable instructions.
    36→- `entire sessions fix`: user-initiated, explicit command.
    37→  - Scans for sessions in pathological states.
    38→  - Shows session info (phase, last seen, shadow branch data, commits with trailers).
    39→  - Lets user choose per session: Condense / Discard / Skip.
    40→- `entire status`: enhanced to show session phases and stuck states.
    41→
    42→**Rationale:**
    43→- Manual approach is simpler, no false positives, no side effects on unrelated sessions.
    44→- Users can determine session liveness better than any heuristic.
    45→- Stale session flagging also catches legitimate "forgotten terminal" scenarios.
    46→
    47→### Drop Catch-Up Checkpoints
    48→
    49→**Decision: Remove catch-up checkpoint logic from the plan.**
    50→
    51→On ACTIVE → ACTIVE transition (UserPromptSubmit while session already ACTIVE due to Ctrl-C/crash):
    52→- Just reset to ACTIVE for the new turn. No special checkpoint creation.
    53→- The interrupted turn's transcript data folds into the next step naturally.
    54→- Accept that the interrupted turn won't have its own rewind point (step).
    55→
    56→**Rationale:**
    57→- An intermediate state from a Ctrl-C or crash is almost never a useful rewind target.
    58→  User would either rewind to the last clean step or continue forward.
    59→- Reconstructing a SaveContext for the interrupted turn is unreliable — pre-prompt state
    60→  may be stale, working directory may have been manually changed since the crash.
    61→- Simplifies Task 3 significantly: no partial-data reconstruction logic.
    62→
    63→### Terminology: Checkpoint vs Step
    64→
    65→**Decision: Clarify and enforce terminology throughout the codebase.**
    66→
    67→- **Checkpoint** = data condensed to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, linked to a user commit
    68→  via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Permanent storage.
    69→- **Step** = shadow branch commit, one per SaveChanges (each agent turn). Rewindable.
    70→  Ephemeral until condensed into a checkpoint.
    71→
    72→A checkpoint may contain multiple steps' worth of data.
    73→
    74→**Renames:**
    75→- `CheckpointCount` → `StepCount` (it counts steps, not checkpoints)
    76→- `SaveChanges` context and related code should use "step" language internally
    77→
    78→### Simplify Transcript Tracking
    79→
    80→**Decision: Replace three overlapping transcript offset fields with two clean ones.**
    81→
    82→Current fields (confusing, overlapping):
    83→- `TranscriptLinesAtStart` — set on first step of checkpoint cycle, from PrePromptState.
    84→  Name is ambiguous ("start" of what?).
    85→- `CondensedTranscriptLines` — updated after condensation. Used as parse offset in Stop
    86→  AND as checkpoint boundary. Dual purpose.
    87→- `PrePromptState.LastTranscriptLineCount` — captured at each UserPromptSubmit. Feeds
    88→  into SaveContext.TranscriptLinesAtStart.
    89→
    90→New fields (single purpose each):
    91→
    92→| Field | Lives In | Set When | Purpose |
    93→|---|---|---|---|
    94→| `CheckpointTranscriptStart` | Session state | Session start (=0) and after each condensation (=current transcript length) | Scopes transcript for checkpoint condensation: "everything since last checkpoint" |
    95→| `stepStart` | PrePromptState (temp file) | Each UserPromptSubmit | Scopes transcript for per-turn file extraction in Stop: "this turn's files" |
    96→
    97→**Key simplification:** Stop only parses this turn's transcript `[stepStart, now]`, not the
    98→full transcript. `FilesTouched` is already accumulated across steps via `mergeFilesTouched`,
    99→so re-parsing old turns was redundant. This makes manual-commit consistent with auto-commit.
   100→
   101→`StepCount` becomes just a counter for display/logging. No more using it as a proxy to
   102→detect "first step of checkpoint cycle" to know when to set transcript offsets. That logic
   103→disappears because `CheckpointTranscriptStart` is set at checkpoint boundaries directly.
   104→
   105→**Lifecycle:**
   106→```
   107→──[checkpoint]──── CheckpointTranscriptStart set here (after condense, or 0 at session start)
   108→    │
   109→    ├── ACTIVE (UserPromptSubmit) ── stepStart captured in PrePromptState
   110→    │     │
   111→    │     └── IDLE (Stop) ── parse [stepStart, now] for this turn's files
   112→    │                         merge into FilesTouched
   113→    │
   114→    ├── ACTIVE (UserPromptSubmit) ── new stepStart
   115→    │     │
   116→    │     └── IDLE (Stop) ── parse [stepStart, now]
   117→    │
   118→──[checkpoint]──── condense transcript [CheckpointTranscriptStart, now]
   119→                   set CheckpointTranscriptStart = now
   120→```
   121→
   122→**Note:** Also subsumes the "CondensedTranscriptLines behavior during deferred condensation"
   123→review item — with the new model, deferred condensation simply means `CheckpointTranscriptStart`
   124→stays where it is until condensation actually happens, and each Stop only parses its own turn.
   125→
   126→### Backward Compatibility During Rollout
   127→
   128→**Decision: Accept. Document it.**
   129→
   130→Existing sessions without a Phase field are treated as IDLE (empty → IDLE). If an agent is
   131→running when the code updates, PostCommit would see IDLE → condense. This is the same bug
   132→that already exists (premature condensation). The update doesn't make it worse; it just
   133→doesn't fix in-flight sessions. Only sessions started after the update get the fix.
   134→
   135→### Defer File Locking
   136→
   137→**Decision: Skip flock-based locking. Defer until storage migration (sqlite or similar).**
   138→
   139→- `syscall.Flock` is POSIX-only, won't work on Windows (which will be needed eventually).
   140→- Also unreliable on NFS.
   141→- Current `Save()` uses atomic write-then-rename, which limits the race window.
   142→- Accept the narrow race condition between concurrent hooks until the storage layer changes.
   143→- **Impact on plan:** PR 1 (File Locking) and Task 1/6 are removed. Plan restructures
   144→  to start with Phase Field directly.
   145→
   146→### Rebase/Merge/Cherry-pick Detection
   147→
   148→**Decision: Detect sequence operations in PostCommit and skip phase transitions.**
   149→
   150→Check for `.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` in PostCommit. If detected, skip
   151→phase transitions and shadow branch migration entirely. Rebase commits aren't "real" agent
   152→commits and shouldn't trigger ACTIVE → ACTIVE_COMMITTED transitions.
   153→
   154→Prevents O(N) shadow branch migrations for N-commit rebases. Not a correctness bug but a
   155→performance concern and source of unnecessary state churn.
   156→
   157→### Fix `git commit --amend` Trailer Preservation
   158→
   159→**Decision: Fix PrepareCommitMsg to preserve trailers on amend. Current bug, needs fixing.**
   160→
   161→**Current bug:** PrepareCommitMsg returns early for `source="commit"` (amend), skipping
   162→entirely. Code to preserve existing trailers (lines 314-322) is unreachable. When user
   163→amends with `-m`, the trailer is lost. Documented in `docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`.
   164→
   165→**Fix with state machine:** For `source="commit"`:
   166→1. Check if message already has `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer → preserve it (done)
   167→2. If no trailer (user used `-m` which stripped it) → check `PendingCheckpointID` in
   168→   session state → re-add the trailer
   169→
   170→`PendingCheckpointID` is the source of truth — it persists in session state across amends.
   171→The trailer is just its manifestation in the commit message. This also handles the case
   172→where the agent amends its own mid-session commits.
   173→
   174→### Auto-Commit Strategy
   175→
   176→**Decision: Don't spend significant time on auto-commit. Keep compatible if easy.**
   177→
   178→Auto-commit has fallen out of favor — agent-controlled (or human) commits produce better
   179→code understandability than auto-commit's granular commits. If phase tracking is naturally
   180→compatible with auto-commit, include it. Otherwise, don't invest effort. The plan should
   181→state this rationale explicitly.
   182→
   183→### Eliminate Two-Package Type Mirroring
   184→
   185→**Decision: Stop duplicating fields between `session.State` and `strategy.SessionState`.**
   186→
   187→Currently `strategy.SessionState` mirrors `session.State` fields with manual conversion
   188→functions. Adding a field to one and forgetting the converter silently loses data.
   189→
   190→Preferred approach: have `strategy.SessionState` embed or directly use `session.State`
   191→instead of duplicating. The `session` package is already separate to avoid import cycles
   192→(`cli` → `strategy`, so `strategy` can't import `cli`). Since `strategy` CAN import
   193→`session`, embedding should work.
   194→
   195→### Shadow Branch Deletion
   196→
   197→**Decision: Simple rule — delete when all sessions sharing the branch are condensed.**
   198→
   199→At steady state (all sessions IDLE/ENDED), PostCommit condenses them all and can delete
   200→the branch. The "check all sessions" logic is only needed for concurrent sessions where
   201→one is ACTIVE_COMMITTED.
   202→
   203→For a single-session workflow (common case), the existing "condense and delete" behavior
   204→is correct. For concurrent sessions, enumerate session states that share the same
   205→BaseCommit + WorktreeID, check if any are ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED.
   206→
   207→### `entire reset` During ACTIVE_COMMITTED
   208→
   209→**Decision: Document. Warn user to wait or run `entire sessions fix` first.**
   210→
   211→If used with `--force`: shadow branch deleted, state cleared. Agent continues → SaveChanges
   212→creates new shadow branch → session state recreated with empty Phase. Self-healing but
   213→produces split data. Document that `--force` during active sessions produces incomplete
   214→checkpoints.
   215→
   216→### Agent Commits Without `-m` Flag
   217→
   218→**Decision: Add test to verify non-interactive behavior.**
   219→
   220→If an agent runs bare `git commit` (no `-m`), prepare-commit-msg opens an editor. In
   221→non-interactive context (agent Bash tool), this would hang. Agents typically use `-m`,
   222→but verify the hook doesn't block. Test with `GIT_EDITOR=true` or similar to confirm
   223→graceful behavior.

    28→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.
    29→// This works even when stdin is redirected (e.g., git commit -m).
    30→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    31→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    32→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    33→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    34→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    35→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    36→	if err != nil {
    37→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    38→		return defaultYes
    39→	}
    40→	defer tty.Close()
    41→
    42→	// Show context if provided
    43→	if context != "" {
    44→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    45→	}
    46→
    47→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    48→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    49→	var hint string
    50→	if defaultYes {

    52→	} else {
    53→		hint = "[y/N]"
    54→	}
    55→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)

    57→	// Read response
    58→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    59→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
    60→	if err != nil {
    61→		return defaultYes
    62→	}
    63→
    64→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
    65→	switch response {
    66→	case "y", "yes":

    68→	case "n", "no":

    70→	default:

   107→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   108→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   109→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   110→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {

   113→		if trimmed == "" {

   159→		return true
   160→	}
   161→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   162→		return true
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   166→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   167→		return true
   168→	}
   169→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   170→		return true
   171→	}
   172→
   173→	return false
   174→}
